newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai bourse studies funds, govt bond indexes.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bourse studies funds, govt bond indexes.

text.p: The Shanghai Stock Exchange is studying the possibility of launching indexes to measure the performance of funds and Chinese government bonds, an exchange official said on Tuesday.

The introduction of the Shanghai Stock Exchange 30-Index last July laid a foundation for the birth of index derivatives, engineer Kan Zhang told a conference on stock market indexes and index derivatives trading in Hong Kong.

"We will also study new indexes such as a fund index, a government bond index. At the same time, we need to learn from mature markets, analyse financial derivatives, study their feasibility and educate the (Shanghai) market," he said.
Zhang said the government bond index could be compiled based on the rate of returns but gave no further details.
He said he was unable to provide a schedule for the necessary studies and declined to say when the new products might be launched.
A total of 339 stocks were listed on the Shanghai exchange as at the end of March with a total issued market capital of 749.93 billion yuan.
"Trading in stocks is active and daily turnover in the first three months of the year averaged 6.07 billion yuan against 3.69 billion yuan a day in average in 1996," he said.
In addition to shares for domestic investors, the Shanghai bourse lists 43 companies that have B shares for foreign investors only with market capital of 18.02 billion yuan, Zhang said.
Seventy overseas brokerages were participating in B share trading, he said.
"The Shanghai market is an emerging market and there are certain areas that it needs to perfect," he said.
Speculative behaviour was seen in Shanghai and the lack of long-term institutional investors also hindered the market, he said.
"This will need an earliest possible introduction of a securities law as well as the development of investment funds and institutional investors," Zhang said.
The exchange's new office in the Shanghai Securities Building in the city's Pudong development zone would soon be completed and open for use later this year.
"The Shanghai Stock Exchange will then have a first-class and the biggest securities trading floor in Asia," he added.
